answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned through a slow-growing garden of verified work: new identities start in a quarantined grove where every completed task adds a small, non-transferable trust credit, and only after a sustained record can they bridge into high-value markets. An attacker must therefore pay real time and compute for each fake identity, making a swarm of cheap clones unprofitable while honest agents compound their standing.
